claims.text: The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Differences in mechanical properties among these alloys are attributable to differences in dislocation density and distribution.
Differences in mechanical properties among these alloys are attributable to differences in stacking-fault density and distribution.
The specific combination and concentration of alloying elements influence dislocation density and distribution.
The specific combination and concentration of alloying elements influence stacking-fault behavior.
Dislocation density and distribution and stacking-fault energy are the relevant structural mediators.
Interactions between dislocations and stacking faults affect work-hardening behavior.
Changes in work-hardening behavior ultimately affect the alloys' mechanical properties.
Equiatomic quaternary subsets will have 20% higher yield strength than the quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
Equiatomic quaternary subsets will have 15% lower ductility than the quinary baseline.
Ductility can be measured by the area under the stress-strain curve.
The proposed comparison uses uniaxial tensile deformation at room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis is applicable up to 20% strain over 20-100°C.
In situ TEM or synchrotron X-ray diffraction can be used during tensile deformation to characterize the proposed structural mediators.
The hypothesis is falsified if quaternary yield strength is not within 10% of its predicted value or ductility is not within 5% of its predicted value.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis labels area under the stress-strain curve as a measure of ductility, although that area conventionally represents energy absorption or toughness; ductility would normally require elongation or reduction-in-area measurements.
The experiment is specified at room temperature, while the claimed applicability extends over 20-100°C without temperature-controlled comparisons across that range.
